paper.title: Optimal Data Driven Resource Allocation under Multi-Armed Bandit Observations

settings.name_in_paper: MAB under side (resource) constraints replenished at a constant rate
unmapped: L deterministic, known, rational per-activation resource costs c^i_j per arm; feasibility requires C_j(n)/n <= c^0_j for every n and every resource j (budget replenished at constant rate c^0_j, surplus carried forward)
the learner knows the costs c^i_j and replenishment rates c^0_j
regret measured against the optimal LP (randomized stationary) policy value n z*(theta)
rewards from a known parametric density family f_i(.|theta_i) with unknown theta_i; all means positive
L < k; arms split into those with c^i_j < c^0_j for all j and those with c^i_j > c^0_j for all j; no cost equals c^0_j

symbols.M_theta: M(theta) = sum_{j in D(theta)} phi_j^B(theta)/K_j(theta): reduced cost of arm j over minimal KL distance K_j to a parameter making j part of the unique optimal LP basis

conditions: policy is feasible and uniformly fast (f-UF): R(theta,n)=o(n^a) for all a>0 and all theta

source.label: th:lb

results.notes: Regret defined through means and expected pull counts => pseudo-regret against the LP-optimal feasible randomized policy.

conditions: condition (C1): lim_{eps->0} J_i(theta,eps)=infinity for relevant non-D arms
condition (C3): P(z^{b_i(hat theta^j, theta_i')} <= z*(theta)-eps for some j<=t)=o(1/t)

source.label: th:ub

results.notes: Matches Theorem 5, so asymptotically optimal among f-UF policies. Section 4 argues (not as formal theorems) that C1-C3 hold for Normal with known variances (K_alpha = phi^2/(2 sigma^2)), Normal with unknown variances, and discrete finite-support distributions.
